transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM); Mark Linton (Silverpine CTO), Rosa Vega (Security Lead), Imran Shah (SRE), Tanya Brooks (PM)

Summary (auto): quick results review from week 3 of pilot, focused on governance / ops items: SSO end-to-end, audit log fidelity, data retention requests, SOC2 artifacts. Agreed next steps for longer dedicated soak and SOC2 docs link.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i think we have a full house — quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Mark Linton: Mark here.
[00:00:08] Rosa Vega: Rosa.
[00:00:10] Imran Shah: Imran, SRE.
[00:00:12] Tanya Brooks: Tanya, product.
[00:00:15] Priya Rao: Priya from Redwood. Diego's on but he had a calendar overlap so he may drop in.
[00:00:20] Alex Chen: cool. agenda — quick perf results, then security ops: SSO, audit logs, retention, SOC two ask, and then next steps. anything to add?
[00:00:30] Mark Linton: nope that's perfect.
[00:00:33] Priya Rao: i'll start with the results slide — last run we did a mix of low-latency hosted traffic and a short dedicated soak. the heading numbers: p95 token latency on hosted was ~210ms for the small convo model and on the dedicated node it dropped to 95ms under 40rps. note, some of the measurements are noisy because we had a short warmup.
[00:00:56] Imran Shah: when you say dedicated node, that's the reserved GP U pool? i guess we meant Redwood Dedicated? the transcript sometimes says 'Dedi' sorry.
[00:01:06] Priya Rao: yes dedicated — Redwood Dedicated pool, one machine. we saw memory pressure around the 8k context step because of kv cache growth, so per-token slowed for a window.
[00:01:20] Rosa Vega: that's important because our retention tests want a large context. what did you have for kv cache eviction behaviour?
[00:01:28] Priya Rao: eviction was conservative — the runtime keeps prefix KV when it's likely to be reused. for your workload with long threads we recommended turning on prefix caching and setting cache window to 12k tokens; that reduced recompute. the caveat is increased memory usage.
[00:01:45] Mark Linton: ok. memory is fine if latency is stable. our biggest blocker is audit logs — we need field-level events for every inference call, user id, prompt hash, model version, and latency buckets. can you produce that?
[00:02:00] Alex Chen: absolutely. we have an audit log schema in the security docs. Priya can link the sample CSV after. for the pilot we can stream logs to your S3 or to the Redwoods managed archive depending on contract.
[00:02:12] Rosa Vega: streaming to S3 is preferable. and we need tamper-evident retention and HSM-backed key rotation. is K M S integrated?
[00:02:21] Priya Rao: yes KMS integration — customer-managed keys via your cloud K M S or our optional H S M. note: there was a past transcription in our doc that said K M S as 'KMSs' so apologies for noise.
[00:02:33] Imran Shah: how granular are the logs? do they include token-level timestamps or just request/response meta?
[00:02:40] Priya Rao: currently we emit request-level rows with request_id, prompt_hash, model_version, start_ts, end_ts, latency_ms, and anonymized user_id. Token-level timestamps are available as an add-on (heavy) — we can enable if you need forensic playback but it will increase storage and cost.
[00:02:58] Rosa Vega: for SOC two evidence we likely don't need token-level right away, but we do need immutable logs and chain-of-custody. can you provide the S O C 2 report or at least the controls mapping?
[00:03:12] Alex Chen: yes we have SOC2 type II report for last year; we'll share the redacted copy and a controls matrix that maps to your auditors. link will be in the follow-up.
[00:03:21] Tanya Brooks: on SSO — we attempted the SAML flow yesterday and it partially worked; we saw assertions but the role mapping didn't line up with our internal RBAC. any ideas?
[00:03:33] Priya Rao: often it's attribute mapping — SAML assertion's 'groups' claim vs 'role' claim. we have a mapping table in the SSO guide. also note our console uses SAML 2.0 but Azure AD sometimes returns group IDs instead of names, which causes mismatch.
[00:03:49] Mark Linton: can we test a few assertion variations in your staging? we'll give you a sample assertion dump.
[00:03:55] Alex Chen: yes please send the dump to security@redwood.ai. We'll schedule a 1-hour SSO pairing session.
[00:04:02] Imran Shah: retention — Silverpine requires 90-day ephemeral logs for dev and 7-year retention for compliance lane. can Redwood support per-namespace retention?
[00:04:13] Priya Rao: yes per-namespace retention is supported for both logs and prompts. we map namespaces to buckets and retention policies. note that for hosted accounts longer retention is an add-on. in Dedicated/Private you control retention on-prem.
[00:04:28] Rosa Vega: and encryption at rest? do you encrypt object store and backups with our keys?
[00:04:33] Alex Chen: yes, object store and snapshot backups can be encrypted with your KMS keys. for Private deployments obviously you manage the keys locally.
[00:04:41] Tanya Brooks: great. any privacy surprises in the transcript data shared earlier? i saw a small PII leak flagged in week one test.
[00:04:49] Priya Rao: we saw a few cases — the prompt sanitization layer we suggested is optional. we can apply PII redaction in the ingestion pipeline for the pilot if you'd like. it will impact retrieval fidelity.
[00:05:02] Mark Linton: we want redaction in dev but full fidelity in compliance lane — can you support both simultaneously?
[00:05:08] Priya Rao: yep you can have policies per namespace: redaction=true for dev, redaction=false for compliance.
[00:05:14] Alex Chen: switching gears — on perf tuning, we proposed quantization changes for the mid-tier model to reduce CPU/GPU usage. any concerns?
[00:05:22] Imran Shah: quantization okay if model outputs are stable. what's your eval for quality drift?
[00:05:27] Priya Rao: we run a regression suite of ~1200 prompts; for the 4-bit profile we saw 0.8% drop in exact-match style metrics and negligible user-facing regression on our human eval. we'll share the eval artifacts.
[00:05:41] Rosa Vega: auditors will ask for change logs of model versions — can you emit versioned artifacts and hashes?
[00:05:47] Priya Rao: yes each model bundle includes a manifest with sha256 hashes, training metadata (if available), and a model_version tag. we'll include those in the audit package.
[00:05:56] Alex Chen: any blockers on your side for the upcoming week?
[00:05:59] Mark Linton: main one is we want a 24h dedicated soak to validate latency and the audit stream. can Redwood run that this week?
[00:06:07] Priya Rao: we can schedule a 24h soak on Thursday; need to confirm capacity. Diego will coordinate. note that soak will produce a large log set so advise retention settings.
[00:06:20] Diego Morales: (joined) sorry for the delay, got the calendar. i can own capacity scheduling.
[00:06:25] Diego Morales: confirm — 24h dedicated soak, stream audit logs to Silverpine S3 with encryption using their KMS, retention 30d for the soak artifacts.
[00:06:35] Imran Shah: 30d is fine for soak artifacts, but we want to validate the long-term retention pipeline — do a follow-up test for 7-year emulation is my ask.
[00:06:44] Priya Rao: OK we can simulate longer retention by stubbing lifecycle rules; for cost we won't actually retain 7 years but we can validate that the lifecycles and immutability flags are set.
[00:06:54] Tanya Brooks: curious: what's the plan if during the soak we hit a fallback event? auto-fallback to smaller model or to hosted?
[00:07:03] Priya Rao: the platform supports policy-based fallback. you can define fallbacks by latency or by capacity. for the soak we recommend no automatic fallback to ensure you see fail modes, unless you'd like otherwise.
[00:07:15] Mark Linton: we want to see fail modes. please run without fallback.
[00:07:19] Alex Chen: noted.
[00:07:21] Rosa Vega: two audit questions: 1) can you provide tamper-evident hashes of logs, and 2) can you provide rsyslog/evt forwarding in near real-time?
[00:07:31] Priya Rao: 1) we support signed log bundles with a chain of custody and sha512 checksums; 2) we can forward to your SIEM via Kafka or syslog connector with <~1 min delay.
[00:07:44] Imran Shah: any compliance gaps we should be aware of?
[00:07:47] Alex Chen: for enterprise packages we cover SOC two, ISO controls; the main gap sometimes is data residency for APAC — we can deploy private in-region or offer dedicated region nodes.
[00:07:59] Mark Linton: we'll keep data in US for now.
[00:08:03] Tanya Brooks: timeline: if soak passes and SSO pairing works, we're targeting internal signoff by 2026-12-20. is that realistic?
[00:08:13] Alex Chen: yes that's realistic. we'll aim to have SOC2 docs, soak results, and SSO success before then.
[00:08:20] Priya Rao: quick note — the SOC two doc we have is from last audit cycle; auditors may want the control implementation details. we'll attach a controls mapping doc.
[00:08:31] Rosa Vega: please redact customer PII in the shared docs.
[00:08:34] Priya Rao: will do.
[00:08:36] Alex Chen: ok let's do a quick recap and owners.
[00:08:40] Alex Chen: recap: 24h dedicated soak (no fallback) -> Priya/Diego to schedule and run; stream audit logs to Silverpine S3 with customer KMS -> Diego/Priya; SSO pairing session -> Alex + Rosa to schedule after receiving assertion dump; send SOC2 and controls mapping -> Alex; PII redaction on shared docs -> Priya; follow-up meeting next week same time.
[00:09:05] Mark Linton: sounds good. one more — pricing note, if we go dedicated at scale what's the reserve discount threshold?
[00:09:13] Alex Chen: i'll send three pricing tiers in the follow-up: small pilot, reserved 3-month, and annual commit with discounts.
[00:09:20] Tanya Brooks: and include cost for audit log storage + token-level logging as an appendix.
[00:09:26] Alex Chen: will do.
[00:09:28] Diego Morales: i'll add a note to the calendar for the soak and include the S3 bucket destination and retention rules.
[00:09:33] Imran Shah: quick aside: are there any known issues with our on-prem firewall and long-lived connections? we saw a couple of reconnections yesterday.
[00:09:41] Priya Rao: long-lived streaming uses websocket keepalives; corporate proxies sometimes kill idle sockets. workaround is shorter heartbeat and retry policy which we can configure.
[00:09:52] Rosa Vega: we'll provision a dedicated egress rule for the soak.
[00:09:56] Alex Chen: cool. any final questions?
[00:09:59] Mark Linton: none from me.
[00:10:01] Tanya Brooks: none.
[00:10:03] Alex Chen: great thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the SOC2 link, soak schedule, and SSO pairing invite.
[00:10:11] Priya Rao: thanks all.

[00:10:20] End of recorded portion — remaining time (~42 min) was working session notes. summary of key artifacts to share:
- SOC2 (redacted) + controls matrix link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-sample (shared after meeting)
- Audit log sample CSV (schema) and streaming guide: https://redwood.ai/docs/audit-logs-streaming
- SSO mapping guide and sample assertion template: https://redwood.ai/docs/sso-guide
- Soak plan spreadsheet (will be shared by Diego) - link: https://drive.company/silverpine/soak-plan.xlsx

Notes from working session (partial):
[00:11:00] Priya Rao: started soak config... increased cache window to 12k... observed memory spike at 18:22 UTC (replay note)
[00:18:20] Imran Shah: captured assertion dump; found groups claim mismatch
[00:29:40] Rosa Vega: confirmed syslog connector works with our SIEM, minor mapping tweaks needed
[00:41:10] Diego Morales: scheduled soak for 2026-12-03 22:00 UTC - 24h
[00:51:55] Alex Chen: meeting adjourned.

Meeting artifacts referenced: audit-schema.csv, soc2-redacted.pdf, soak-results-template.csv
